transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

Um… hi. I guess I’m here because I’ve been getting kind of stuck on how my face looks. It’s probably not as big a deal as it feels, but I keep thinking the left side looks… off, like my nose or jaw is crooked, especially in ID photos or on the camera for online classes.

People tell me they don’t really see it, so maybe I’m overreacting, but I can’t stop feeling like everyone in the CNC lab notices that first, before they notice anything about my work. I’m not sure if that’s the right kind of thing to come in for, but it’s been hard to shake.
How much does this concern about your face bother you during the day?

It bothers me… probably more than I want to admit. I try to tell myself it’s just a bad camera angle or an ID photo thing, but then I keep coming back to it during the day.

Like in the CNC lab, I’ll be trying to focus on my work, and I’m still thinking, “Do they notice the left side of my face? Does my nose or jaw look crooked?” Even when people say they don’t see anything, it doesn’t really settle it for me. I feel kind of embarrassed saying that, because I know it might sound small, but it takes up a lot of space in my head.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, taking pictures, or adjusting your face, to try to fix or examine how your face looks?

Yeah… I mean, I do check, probably more than I should. Before I leave for school I can get kind of stuck in the bathroom mirror, and then I’ll use my phone camera too, just to see if it looks as crooked as I think it does.

I’ll mess with my hair or change shirts, like maybe one hides the angle better. And I’ll ask my mom, “Does it look weird?” even though I know she’s probably tired of me asking. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but sometimes it goes on long enough that I’m late or I miss lab, or I get there and I’m already kind of wiped out and can’t focus that well.
Do you think the asymmetry on your face is something others notice easily, or do you believe it’s something that only you can really see?

I guess… I know people say they don’t notice it, so maybe it’s more obvious to me than to everyone else. But it doesn’t feel that way in the moment.

Like, in ID photos or on the online class camera, I feel like the left side of my face looks wrong—my nose and jaw look crooked—and then I get this feeling that people in the CNC lab must be seeing it right away, before they notice anything I’m doing. I know that probably sounds like I’m assuming a lot, but it’s hard for me not to feel like it’s obvious.
Do you feel that your concern about your face is part of a bigger pattern where you often worry about how you look in general, or is it mostly about this specific asymmetry that you notice in photos?

It’s… mostly that specific thing, I think. The left side of my face looking off. Like my nose and jaw seem crooked to me in ID photos or when I’m on the online class camera.

I don’t want to make it sound like I’m obsessed with every part of how I look, because that feels kind of… I don’t know, embarrassing. But this one thing gets stuck in my head. Even when people tell me they don’t see it, I still feel like people in the CNC lab are noticing it before they notice my work. Does that make sense?

Has this concern about the left side of your face ever caused you to avoid certain situations, like going to the CNC lab, participating in class, or interacting with others, because you feel too self-conscious?

Yeah… I mean, not all the time, but it has happened. I’ve missed some CNC labs and shop shifts because I just couldn’t get myself out the door. I know that sounds bad—I’m not trying to make excuses. I just get stuck thinking everyone’s going to notice my face, and then I wait too long, and then it feels impossible to go.

My faculty mentor actually said my work placement could be in jeopardy if I keep missing things, so… it’s more serious than I’d like to admit.

And I stopped playing soccer and volunteering too. I kind of told people I was busy, but really I just didn’t want to be in places where people would be looking at me. Does that answer what you mean?

Do you find yourself doing certain mental exercises or routines—like analyzing photos, comparing images, or mentally rehearsing interactions—because you’re trying to figure out if your face looks okay or to prevent feeling embarrassed?

Yeah… I guess I do some of that. I don’t know if I’d call it a routine exactly, but before I leave for school I can get kind of stuck checking my face in the bathroom mirror, and then on my phone camera too, to see if it looks different.

Sometimes I’ll fix my hair a bunch, or change shirts because I think one makes the angle of my face stand out less. And I’ll ask my mom if it looks weird, even though I know that probably gets annoying.

I try not to let it take over, but sometimes it goes on long enough that I miss lab, or I do make it there but I’m already so drained that I can’t really focus. I feel stupid saying that, but… yeah, that happens.

When you’re worried about how the left side of your face looks, do you feel driven to do certain things—like checking mirrors, changing your clothes, or asking others—because you feel anxious and want to make the worry go away?

Yeah… I think that’s fair to say. I don’t do it because I’m trying to be difficult or vain or anything. It’s more like I get this anxious feeling and I feel like I have to check, just to calm down.

Before I leave for school, I’ll get stuck looking in the bathroom mirror, then checking my phone camera, and sometimes fixing my hair or changing shirts because I think it hides the angle better. And I’ll ask my mom if it looks weird, even though I know she’s probably tired of hearing it.

I try to keep it quick, but sometimes it takes so long that I miss lab, or I get there feeling completely drained and can’t really focus. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

Do you feel that your concern about your face leads you to do things like constantly checking your appearance, changing your clothes, or avoiding certain situations to prevent feeling upset or to stop others from noticing what you’re worried about?

Yeah… yes, I think it does. I mean, I try to tell myself I’m just being careful before I leave, but it turns into checking my face in the bathroom mirror, then using my phone camera too.

And I’ll mess with my hair or change shirts if I think it makes that side less noticeable. Sometimes I ask my mom if it looks weird, even though I know I’ve asked before.

It’s embarrassing to admit, but sometimes I get caught up in it long enough that I miss lab, or I do get there and I’m just… wiped out and can’t focus. I’m not trying to make it sound worse than it is, but that does happen.
Has this concern about your face ever made it hard for you to function in areas of your life outside of school, like with friends, family, or in everyday activities?

Yeah… it has, I guess. Not just school.

I used to play soccer and do some volunteering, and I kind of stopped going. I tell people I’m busy, which is partly true, but really I just don’t want to be around people if I feel like they’re going to look at my face.

And with the CNC stuff… I’ve missed labs and even shop shifts because I couldn’t get myself out the door. My faculty mentor said my work placement could be in jeopardy if it keeps happening, so… yeah, I know it’s becoming a problem. I don’t want to make excuses, but that’s what’s been happening.

Do you feel like you have to repeat certain behaviors, like checking your face multiple times or asking the same question over and over, because it doesn’t feel quite right or you’re afraid something bad will happen if you don’t?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t know if it’s like “something bad will happen” exactly, but it just doesn’t feel okay to leave until I’ve checked enough.

Like before school, I’ll look in the bathroom mirror, then check my phone camera, and if the left side looks off I’ll fix my hair or change shirts to try to cover that angle better. And then sometimes I’ll ask my mom if it looks weird, even though I know I already asked.

I know that probably sounds repetitive. I try not to make it a big thing, but sometimes I get stuck doing it long enough that I miss lab, or I get there and I’m so worn out from it that I can’t focus. Does that answer what you mean?
Has the concern about the left side of your face ever caused problems in your relationships, schoolwork, or other areas of your life, even outside of the CNC lab or soccer?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I’m just falling apart or anything, but it has caused problems.

I’ve missed CNC labs and some shop shifts because I just couldn’t get myself out the door when I felt like the left side looked bad. And my faculty mentor told me my work placement could be in jeopardy if I keep missing things, so that’s… not great.

Outside of that, I stopped playing soccer and volunteering too. I usually tell people I’m busy, but honestly it’s more that I don’t want people looking at me. I know that probably sounds excessive, but yeah, it’s affected more than just one area.
